subject: Egress path switchover guidance and post-incident triage
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: ops@optifood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 08:32:00 +0000
Subject: Egress path switchover guidance and post-incident triage

Hi Anika —

Quick update from the infra side: at 08:12 UTC we observed sustained packet loss on the primary egress path serving EU customers that affected request completion rates for some tenants. Our control plane initiated an automated path switchover to the secondary egress route at 08:15 UTC which restored the majority of customer traffic. You may have seen elevated latencies and some 503s during the window.

What we did
- Detected abnormal egress loss on eu-1 -> upstream peering
- Automated route switch to eu-2 (alternate backbone) at 08:15 UTC
- Enabled extra capacity on eu-2 and warmed KV caches for hot tenants

Impact summary for OptiFood (what we saw in your telemetry)
- Short spike of failed requests (approx 3–7% of requests) between 08:10–08:18 UTC
- Median latency increased by ~120ms for ~10 minutes post-switchover while caches warmed
- No data loss; KV caches were rehydrated from persisted state

Immediate ask (what we need from you)
1) Run the two quick validation checks in the attached validation_checklist.csv and reply with the results.
2) Run this curl test from a client in your EU region: curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health?tenant=optifood -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
3) Confirm whether you need us to fail traffic to US region temporarily (we can enable geo-fallback within 30m) or keep routing on eu-2.

Attachments: reroute_instructions_v1.pdf, validation_checklist.csv, incident_triage_notes.txt

We’ll schedule a short post-incident review tomorrow; Ben, Marissa, Karthik — please see for commercial and CS follow-ups.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Site Reliability Lead, Redwood Inference

From: Anika Rao <ops@optifood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:10:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Egress path switchover guidance and post-incident triage

Thanks Olga — appreciate the quick note. A couple quick questions: 

- We saw multiple client retries and some user-facing errors during the 08:10–08:20 window. Can you confirm whether session affinity/sticky routing is preserved when the path switches? Will in-flight requests be retried or dropped?
- Any ETA on the RCA and timeline for a permanent fix?
- Can you confirm whether Redwood will apply a service credit for the outage window (we typically request credit for interruptions that affect availability)?

We ran the curl test and saw ~1% failed connections from our EU testers; full checklist submission will follow shortly. If there’s a recommended temporary mitigation (e.g., reduced concurrency or a config toggle on our side) let us know.

—Anika
Anika Rao
Ops Lead, OptiFood Inc.

Subject: Re: Egress path switchover guidance and post-incident triage

Hi Anika — thanks for the quick check and the questions. Short answers first then detail: 

- Session affinity: preserved. Routing policy keeps sticky flow based on connection hash; in-flight tokens are retried by the proxy where possible, but a small number of requests that were mid-flight at the moment of path packet loss may have been dropped — that aligns with the ~1% you saw.
- RCA & timeline: we’ve identified a flapping peering session on a 3rd-party transit and are collecting vendor BGP logs; expect an RCA draft by EOD tomorrow (22 May) and a final postmortem by 28 May.
- Credits: Ben is looped for the commercial follow-up; we’ll propose a partial credit for the impacted window and handle through the normal billing remediation flow.

Immediate mitigations you can take (optional)
- Reduce token concurrency for the 10 minutes after any future switchover to allow caches to warm: set X-CONCURRENCY-LIMIT on your side to 80% for short windows.
- Retry policy: ensure client retries are idempotent for short windows (we also apply safe retries where possible).

I ran an internal sweep and attached a short triage note (incident_triage_notes.txt) with the timelines and traces we have so far. If you want, we can enable temporary geo-fallback to US for your tenant (latency will increase ~70–120ms but availability will be higher). Please reply with preference.

Olga
